html:
Mali is a large landlocked country in West Africa, reaching from the Sahara in the north to the farmland along the Niger River in the south, with its capital at Bamako. The map shows its area from 1945, when it was the colony of French Sudan.

It is named after the medieval Mali Empire of Mansa Musa, and its land held Timbuktu and Djenné. France conquered the region in the late 1800s and ruled it as part of French West Africa. In 1960, the Year of Africa, it became independent, briefly in a federation with Senegal, then alone under the socialist president Modibo Keïta.

A military coup in 1968 brought Moussa Traoré, who ruled until protests and a coup in 1991. Mali then held elections and was seen as a model democracy for twenty years. In 2012 a Tuareg rebellion and jihadist groups took the north, and French troops intervened in 2013; see the Mali War. Army officers seized power in 2020 and 2021, expelled the French, and turned to Russia for help. Gold and cotton are its main exports.
